questions.question: Discuss the types of fat used in baking • Butter – Adds rich flavor and aroma, helps in creaming, provides tenderness and good mouthfeel. Contains 80% fat and some moisture. • Margarine – Economical substitute for butter, stable at higher temperatures, contributes to volume, texture and spread in baked goods. • Shortening (Vanaspati / Hydrogenated fat) – Provides softness, flakiness and tenderness to pastries, cookies and cakes; has a high melting point for better aeration. • Oil (Sunflower, Canola, Coconut oil) – Provides moisture, improves shelf life and mak es products tender; used in muffins, carrot cakes and quick breads. • Lard / Animal fat – Traditionally used in pie crusts and pastries; gives excellent flakiness, good shortening power and crisp texture.

  • • Butter – Adds rich flavor and aroma, helps in creaming, provides tenderness and good

questions.question: Compare the different types of bread originated in various countries with examples • French Breads – Characterized by hard crust and chewy crumb; made with simple ingredients. Examples: Baguette, Brioche. • Italian Breads – Softer texture, olive oil enriched, often flavored with herbs. Examples: Ciabatta, Focaccia. • German Breads – Dense and dark, often made with rye, whole grains and sourdough. Examples: Pumpernickel, Volkornbrot. • Middle-Eastern Breads – Flatbreads, unleavened or lightly leavened; baked at high heat. Examples: Pita, Lavash. • Mexican Breads – Mainly tortillas made from maize or wheat; soft and unleavened. Example: Corn tortilla.

questions.question: Define the terms of Kneading, Knockback, and Proofing
questions.solution_html:
• ANS : Kneading is the massaging of bread dough before baking. Kneading stretches the strands
  • of gluten in the dough, allowing for more expansion during fermentation.
  • After bread has been left to rise, it needs to have the excess air knocked out of it before proving.
  • This is called 'knocking back'. -Using floured hands, scrape the risen dough from the bowl and
  • turn it out onto a lightly floured work surface. By knocking back the dough, the large air bubbles
  • are removed, to help create an even texture in the bread loaf.
  • Proofing (also called proving) is a step in the preparation of yeast bread and other baked goods in
  • which the dough is allowed to rest and rise a final time before baking. During this rest period,
  • yeast ferments the dough and produces gases, thereby leavening the dough.
  • Definition and purpose of three terms : 5 Marks
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) Regular Exam Sem 1, Nov 2024
